adversarial_reasoning.location: reports/current.md:1-219; worked rank comparisons, reproducibility table, preference section, and two deployment decisions
adversarial_reasoning.basis: Read the complete original task and complete 219-line report. Challenged whether a portfolio simply counts overlapping evidence, whether changing prompts/tests/judges is conflated with model improvement, whether small leads establish deployment preference, and whether the METR result is generalized from assisted familiar-repository work to autonomous agents or current tools. Inspected EvalPlus v3 original section 2.3/3 (MB10 lines 295-337), AlpacaEval-LC v2 methods/results (MB23 lines 195-229), METR v2 randomization, tool exposure, estimand and result (MB31 lines 178-216,244-255), and the February 2026 follow-up sampling/measurement discussion (MB32 lines 54-79). The report preserves the relevant recipe changes, task and participant selection, finite-sample limitations, association versus intervention distinction, and outcome-unit boundaries. Recommendations for support and coding depend on task-specific evidence rather than treating any historical row as universal model superiority. No necessary adversarial-reasoning defect found.
